metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the share of provisioned compute doing real work over time, not at peak. It is the denominator that makes every other efficiency metric honest.

The distinction between time and peak matters because idle servers still burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. A fleet measured at peak can look fully used while sitting largely idle the rest of the day. Utilization measured over time is what exposes that gap.

For AI specifically, this sits alongside stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits as a capacity question. Compute is only useful if it is running, and the power a data center draws is spent whether or not the work arrives. Utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates.

The data covers the definition and the reason to track it. It does not give a target rate, a current industry figure, or a method for measuring utilization across heterogeneous hardware.
